summary: The round-two changes repair the prior filename, logging, output-isolation, and duplicate-result-key failures. Two major identification problems remain: the legibility heterogeneity comparison is mechanically confounded by the share of records receiving treatment, and the before/after validation comparison changes the middle-initial yardstick. The most important fix is to condition or standardize the legibility results on treatment exposure before describing them as effectiveness on hard-to-read records.

findings.title: The target-only legibility gradient mechanically compares districts with different treatment shares
findings.location: CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:27-40, CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:73, CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:111, CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:138, MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:47-54, MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:111-114, CODE/compute_legibility_quartiles.do:43-47, CODE/compute_legibility_quartiles.do:64-87
findings.what_the_code_does: The code defines `congruent=namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast`, defines district `legibility=mean(congruent)`, and defines targets as the exact complement, `!(namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast)`. Target mode then substitutes model names only for those target records, while the quartile analysis compares all-record `linked_after/linked_before` gains across quartiles of `legibility`. It therefore compares districts with systematically different shares of records whose names were changed, rather than holding treatment exposure fixed.
findings.why_it_matters: A larger all-record linkage gain in low-legibility districts can arise even if the model has the same effect on every treated record, simply because those districts contain more treated records. The result supports a policy-level statement about districts with more Ancestry–FamilySearch disagreements, but it does not identify greater effectiveness on intrinsically hard-to-read records.
findings.how_to_check: In the pre-collapse data, generate `target=1-congruent`, calculate the enumeration-district mean of `target`, and run `corr legibility target_share`; then reproduce each quartile's linkage gain using only `target==1` and compare it with the current all-record gain. Also tabulate target share by `leg_q`.
findings.suggested_fix: Report target share in every legibility quartile and estimate gains among target records or after standardizing quartiles to a common target share. Describe `legibility` as transcription-source agreement unless an independent image-legibility measure is available.

findings.title: The share-validated comparison changes the 1940 middle-initial yardstick along with the links
findings.what_the_code_does: For the baseline link file, `validated_before=mi1930==mi1940` uses Ancestry-derived 1940 initials. After dropping those fields and merging the target-only link file, `validated_after=mi1930==mi1940` uses the model initial on target records and Ancestry's initial elsewhere. Thus both the linked pairs and the variable used to validate them change; the intended link-quality comparison would hold the validation transcription fixed.
findings.why_it_matters: The tracked target results show 65.41% before versus 83.62% after when each version uses its own 1940 initial, but only 75.69% after when the same Ancestry 1940 initial is used for scoring. Almost eight percentage points of the apparent target-sample improvement therefore comes from changing the yardstick, not solely from changing which pairs are linked.
findings.how_to_check: Rerun `MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do` and compare the `Share validated, MI` and `Share validated, Ancestry 1940 MI` rows for target records, already shown at `MATCHING/results/tgt_linkage_abe.md:29-37`. Apply the same fixed-initial calculation by legibility quartile.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one fixed 1940 middle-initial source for both before and after columns, while clearly acknowledging that it is not ground truth. Retain the own-source calculation only as a separately labelled sensitivity result and prioritize independently verified pairs where available.

review_limits: No paper or slide draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code could not compare prose with generated numbers or labels.

The Stata pipeline was not executed; `temp_tgt.dta` and the new target figure outputs did not yet exist. Runtime conclusions rely on source, installed Stata 15 documentation, and existing tracked scoring results.
The multi-gigabyte external `.dta` inputs were existence-checked but not opened, so their schemas, key uniqueness, and exact target-mode quartile results were not independently verified.
The review was scoped to the uncommitted working tree and immediate link-producing and scoring dependencies, not the full historical pipeline.
